findings.title: SQL Injection in /rest/products/search
findings.description: CWE-89 SQL Injection. The search endpoint concatenates user input directly into a SQL query. Payload ' or '1'='1 returns all products instead of search results, demonstrating boolean-based SQLi with trivial bypass.
steps: Observe response returns all products with status success
findings.evidence: HTTP 200 with full product list returned when injecting ' or '1'='1 in q parameter.

findings.title: IDOR: Authenticated user can list and access any user account via /api/Users
findings.description: CWE-639 IDOR / CWE-284 Broken Access Control. The /api/Users/ and /api/Users/<id> endpoints only verify that a valid JWT is present but do not enforce ownership. An authenticated customer (jim@juice-sh.op) was able to retrieve the full list of users including admin email addresses and roles, and individual admin account details.
findings.evidence: Response returned id=1 admin@juice-sh.op role=admin among all users, with only a customer JWT.

findings.title: JWT payload exposes password hash and user role
findings.description: CWE-200 Information Exposure. The JWT token returned by /rest/user/login embeds the user's MD5 password hash, role, and other internal fields in the unencrypted payload. An attacker with XSS, log access, or browser history can read these claims.

findings.title: [ZAP] Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set
findings.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) is an added layer of security that helps to detect and mitigate certain types of attacks, including Cross Site Scripting (XSS) and data injection attacks. These attacks are used for everything from data theft to site defacement or distribution of malware. findings.title: [ZAP] Session ID in URL Rewrite
findings.description: URL rewrite is used to track user session ID. The session ID may be disclosed via cross-site referer header. In addition, the session ID might be stored in browser history or server logs. | CWE-598 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, put session ID in a cookie. To be even more secure consider using a combination of cookie and URL rewrite.

findings.title: [ZAP] Re-examine Cache-control Directives
findings.description: The cache-control header has not been set properly or is missing, allowing the browser and proxies to cache content. For static assets like css, js, or image files this might be intended, however, the resources should be reviewed to ensure that no sensitive content will be cached. | CWE-525 | WASC-13
steps: Solução: For secure content, ensure the cache-control HTTP header is set with "no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate". If an asset should be cached consider setting the directives "public, max-age, immutable".

findings.title: [ZAP] Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set
findings.description: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) is a web security policy mechanism whereby a web server declares that complying user agents (such as a web browser) are to interact with it using only secure HTTPS connections (i.e. HTTP layered over TLS/SSL). HSTS is an IETF standards track protocol and is specified in RFC 6797. | CWE-319 | WASC-15
steps: Solução: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to enforce Strict-Transport-Security.

findings.title: [ZAP] Session Management Response Identified

Mas faltam parênteses de fechamento do WHERE? O WHERE ((name LIKE '%')) fecha os dois parênteses internos e o externo? name LIKE '%' tem um (, depois %')) fecha os dois? Original WHERE ((... OR ...)
